events.blurb: Giotto paints the Arena Chapel in Padua, giving sacred figures weight, grief, and physical presence. The frescoes break from flat Byzantine style and open the Renaissance in painting.
events.label: Giotto, Arena Chapel, 1305

events.blurb: Duccio completes the Maestà, the great double-sided altarpiece for Siena Cathedral, blending Byzantine gold with a new tenderness and narrative detail.
events.label: Duccio, Maestà, 1311

events.blurb: Lorenzo Ghiberti, a young goldsmith, wins the competition for the Florence Baptistery's north doors with his Sacrifice of Isaac. The contest is often called the opening event of Renaissance art.
events.label: Ghiberti wins the doors, 1401

events.blurb: Filippo Brunelleschi raises the dome of Florence Cathedral without scaffolding, using a herringbone brick pattern and a double shell. It remains the largest masonry dome ever built.
events.label: Brunelleschi's dome, 1420-1436

events.blurb: Masaccio paints the Brancacci Chapel frescoes in Florence, using single-point perspective and stark, unidealized bodies. He dies at twenty-seven, but his work becomes the textbook for the next generation.
events.label: Masaccio, Brancacci Chapel, c. 1425

events.blurb: Donatello casts his bronze David, the first freestanding nude male sculpture since antiquity and the first unsupported standing bronze of the Renaissance.
events.label: Donatello, bronze David, c. 1440

events.blurb: Leon Battista Alberti finishes the facade of the Palazzo Rucellai, applying classical pilasters and proportions to a Florentine townhouse and fixing the grammar of Renaissance architecture.
events.label: Alberti, Palazzo Rucellai, 1451

events.blurb: Botticelli paints the Primavera, a pagan allegory of spring crowded with classical gods, almost certainly for a Medici villa. It is the Renaissance's fullest embrace of mythology as subject matter.
events.label: Botticelli, Primavera, c. 1482

events.blurb: Botticelli paints the Birth of Venus, placing a nude classical goddess at the center of a major work for the first time in a thousand years.
events.label: Botticelli, Birth of Venus, c. 1485

events.blurb: Leonardo finishes the Last Supper in Milan, arranging the apostles in four groups of three around Christ and using perspective to make the painted room continue the monks' refectory.
events.label: Leonardo, Last Supper, 1498

events.blurb: Leonardo begins the portrait of Lisa Gherardini in Florence. He carries it with him for the rest of his life, and it becomes the most famous painting in the world.
events.label: Leonardo begins the Mona Lisa, 1503

events.blurb: Michelangelo completes the David, carved from a single rejected block of marble, and Florence sets it before the Palazzo Vecchio as a symbol of the republic.
events.label: Michelangelo, David, 1504

events.blurb: Pope Julius II lays the foundation stone for the new St Peter's Basilica, designed by Bramante. The rebuilding takes 120 years and becomes the architectural project of the age.
events.label: St Peter's rebuilding, 1506-1626

events.blurb: Raphael completes the School of Athens in the Vatican's Stanza della Segnatura, gathering the philosophers of antiquity under a vast perspectival vault, Plato and Aristotle at the vanishing point.
events.label: Raphael, School of Athens, 1511

events.blurb: Michelangelo completes the Sistine Chapel ceiling, nine scenes from Genesis framed by prophets and sibyls, painted lying on scaffolding over four years.
events.label: Michelangelo, Sistine Ceiling, 1512

events.blurb: Titian completes the Assumption of the Virgin for Santa Maria Gloriosa dei Frari in Venice, a towering altarpiece that makes color and light, rather than Florentine line, the basis of painting.
events.label: Titian, Assumption, 1518

events.blurb: Michelangelo completes the Last Judgment on the Sistine altar wall, a writhing mass of risen bodies that shocks Rome with its nudity and inaugurates Mannerism's successor age.
events.label: Michelangelo, Last Judgment, 1541

events.blurb: Andrea Palladio's Teatro Olimpico in Vicenza, the oldest surviving indoor theater, is completed after his death. Its forced-perspective streets behind the stage become the model for theater design.
events.label: Palladio, Teatro Olimpico, 1585

events.blurb: Caravaggio completes the Calling of Saint Matthew in San Luigi dei Francesi, Rome, plunging a tavern scene into darkness cut by a single shaft of light. The chiaroscuro shocks Rome and founds Baroque painting.
events.label: Caravaggio, Calling of St Matthew, 1600

events.blurb: Bernini completes Apollo and Daphne for Cardinal Borghese, marble caught mid-transformation: bark creeping up Daphne's legs, leaves sprouting from her fingers. Baroque sculpture has arrived.
events.label: Bernini, Apollo and Daphne, 1625
